description: We're secondary school students who like making games and motivating young children to engage or learn scientific stuff in space without having to understand complex concept or basics.
summary: Our project aims to develop an entertaining and educational game set in a lunar outpost, primarily targeting children aged 7–12 while welcoming older players. The game introduces basic physics and astronomy concepts to help players understand their importance in scientific discoveries and future space exploration. Players experience life on the Moon by managing essential resources such as food, power, and radiation exposure. Through interactive controls, they make decisions that affect resource usage, and research missions. Each choice leads to different consequences, highlighting how actions can influence both immediate situations and long-term outcomes. Decision-making is a key part of the gameplay, encouraging players to think carefully before acting. Players also develop problem-solving, critical thinking, and adaptability skills. By experiencing astronauts' challenges, they gain scientific knowledge, understand the importance of responsible choices, and develop curiosity about space exploration and future careers in science and technology.Thus it benefits the young player to learn about critical thinking and thinking about their action with the outcome before doing it.
details: Our project is mostly targeted to audiences between 7-12 but older audiences may also play. Players will experience living in a lunar outpost while managing resources given to them such as managing food supply, monitor radiation exposure, and preserving power usage. The game will include buttons to engage the player so they can manage their resource consumption with an aftermath, forcing them to learn how their first-hand decision can impact the global world and reshape the future space exploration by relying on second-hand information they learnt from their own individual research or education. We used Godot to develop our project and focused highly on gameplay and technical constraints.
